name: Vancura defence (rook pawn on the sixth or below)

plans.label: Rook on the sixth, off the pawn's file
plans.description: Place the rook on the defender's third rank attacking the rook pawn sideways from far away, on one of the middle files, so the pawn cannot advance without walking out of one attack into another.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Attack the pawn from the side', whose success was holding. It is now the set-up: Black's rook stands on the sixth rank in the middle files, from where it attacks a rook pawn along the rank rather than sitting in front of it. The middle-file restriction is what separates the Vancura rook from a passive one on the pawn's own file. Original success note: 'Holding is an outcome and has no structural signature here.'

plans.label: Side checks when the king approaches
plans.description: When the attacking king walks over to shield its pawn, the same rook checks it away along the files — near the edge there is no shelter from side checks that also keep the pawn attacked.

success.note: The checking geometry is not rules arithmetic.

plans.label: Set-up on the board with the pawn still short of the seventh
plans.description: The defence must be built while the pawn stands on the sixth or lower: the rook is already on the sixth rank in the middle files and no White pawn has reached the seventh.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Reach the set-up before the seventh', whose success was move order. It is now the two facts move order produces, read together: the Vancura rook is on the sixth in the middle files and no White pawn has reached the seventh. A census cannot see the order they arrived in, only that both hold at once. Original success note: 'Set-up timing is move order, not a census.'

plans.label: Rook behind, king across
plans.description: Keep the rook behind the pawn, not in front of it, and march the king toward the pawn trying to shield the side checks and break the rank attack; the winning attempt is king and rook sheltering each other.

success.note: The pawn on the seventh ends the Vancura set-up; what follows is a different, often still drawn, story the arithmetic cannot judge.

watch: Only the a- and h-file census fires here, matching the runtime technique index, which names Vancura for rook pawns; a knight-file pawn is a different family.
The defining placement — defending rook attacking the pawn sideways from its third rank — is rook geometry this vocabulary cannot express; the trigger names the family.
Extra pawns are not excluded by the census; count them.
Colour convention: White is authored as the stronger/attacking side. Mirror the plans when the colours are reversed; the trigger fires only for the White-side census.
typicalMistakes: Leaving the defending rook passive in front of the pawn — the one placement that loses the checking set-up entirely.
Starting the side-attack set-up one tempo late, after the pawn has reached the seventh.
Walking the defending king toward the pawn to help, when the defence needs it exactly where it is, out of the way of the checks.
As the attacker, advancing the pawn while the rook still stands in front of it.
